identity.name: ANLON HEALTHCARE LIMITED
identity.industry: Pharma API & Intermediates (NSAID specialist) + emerging Fine/Specialty Chemicals & CDMO

summary.oneLiner: Anlon delivered a strong FY26 (total income +43% to INR 172 cr, EBITDA +48% to INR 47.8 cr, PAT +42% to INR 29.1 cr) and bolted on three acquisitions (Apiqo, Bizotic, and FY27's Remember Pharma) to build a backward-integrated NSAID-API + intermediates + CDMO + formulations platform — but Q4 PAT fell YoY (INR 11.1 cr vs INR 16.7 cr) as a raw-material/solvent cost spike ("war situation", prices >2x) hit B2B contracts already priced at old rates, compressing margins. The story now hinges on (a) repricing customers and restoring the ~25-30% EBITDA band, (b) ramping consolidated capacity (1,400-1,600 MTPA) plus a new INR 130 cr Rajkot greenfield (commissioning ~Q1 FY28) toward a 30% revenue CAGR (FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr, FY28 ~INR 700-800 cr), and (c) fixing a stretched working-capital cycle (receivables ~200+ days, consolidated cash flow at -INR 47 cr).

currentContext.strategies: Board did not recommend any dividend on equity shares for FY26 in order to conserve resources, and no amount was transferred to the general reserves account during the year; the Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy per the Listing Regulations.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the company expanded inorganically by acquiring 67.48% equity shareholding in Apiqo Organics Private Limited (subsidiary w.e.f. January 09, 2026) and 56.67% equity shareholding in Bizotic Life Science Private Limited (subsidiary w.e.f. March 20, 2026).

risks.risk: No company-specific risk register is disclosed anywhere in the report
risks.note: Risk Management is covered by a single generic paragraph — 'a well-defined risk management mechanism covering the risk mapping and trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact and risk mitigation process is in place' — with no risk named, quantified or ranked. The Risk Management Committee met only twice in FY26 (11-11-2025 and 09-02-2026), and the Board states that 'the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report as stipulated in Section 34 of the Listing Regulations is not applicable to the Company', so the BRSR material-issues table that normally serves as an Indian issuer's risk register does not exist here. An investor has no disclosed view of what management thinks can go wrong.

risks.risk: Promoter-executive sits on the committees meant to oversee him
risks.note: Mr. Punitkumar Rameshbhai Rasadia is Chairman & Managing Director and is simultaneously a member of the Audit Committee and Chairman of the Risk Management Committee, and a member of the Internal Complaints Committee. Ms. Mamata Punitkumar Rasadia chairs the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and sits on the NRC. Only two Non-Executive Independent Directors (Mr. Krishna Murty Kannepalli, Mr. Anandbhai Natwerlal Katkoria) recur across the oversight committees, so independent challenge rests on a very narrow base.

risks.risk: First year as a listed company, with IPO proceeds deployment undisclosed
risks.note: The Company completed its IPO during the year — a fresh issue of 1,33,00,000 equity shares at Rs.91 per share aggregating Rs.121.03 crore, listed on NSE and BSE on September 03, 2025. FY26 is therefore the first partial year of listed-company reporting, and the routed sections carry no statement on how the fresh-issue proceeds have been utilised or deviated versus objects.

risks.risk: Two majority-owned subsidiaries acquired in the closing quarter, with no comparatives
risks.note: The Company acquired 67.48% of Apiqo Organics Private Limited w.e.f. January 09, 2026 and 56.67% of Bizotic Life Science Private Limited w.e.f. March 20, 2026. The Board itself notes that 'comparative figure of Financial Year 2024-25 is not applicable' for the consolidated column. Both stakes are majority-but-partial, so integration execution, minority interests, and a consolidated base that reflects only weeks of ownership all sit outside any historical track record.

risks.risk: Operations funded on bank cash credit and term loan facilities
risks.note: Under Finance, the Board states that 'company has been utilizing cash credit/term loan facilities from the Bank and the Company has been regular in payment of interest as well as instalments as per schedule to Banks'. Working capital and expansion therefore depend on continued bank sanction and renewal; no alternative funding line, rating, or headroom is disclosed.

risks.risk: No dividend, explicitly to conserve resources
risks.note: 'In order to conserve resources, the Board of Directors has not recommended any dividend on the Equity Shares for the financial year.' Despite a Dividend Distribution Policy being on the books, all cash is retained, so shareholder return depends entirely on the quality of reinvestment — including into the two newly acquired subsidiaries — rather than on any payout.

risks.risk: Related-party transactions in a family-held board, disclosed only by reference
risks.note: Related party transactions were significant enough to require Form AOC-2 (Annexure-II), which is triggered by contracts needing disclosure, while the Board asserts all were at arm's length and in the ordinary course. Given that the Chairman & MD, a Non-Executive Director and a Whole Time Director occupy the committee seats, and that the Audit Committee that clears such transactions includes the Managing Director, the RPT stream is a structural watch item rather than a settled one.

The story now hinges on (a) repricing customers and restoring the ~25-30% EBITDA band, (b) ramping consolidated capacity (1,400-1,600 MTPA) plus a new INR 130 cr Rajkot greenfield (commissioning ~Q1 FY28) toward a 30% revenue CAGR (FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr, FY28 ~INR 700-800 cr), and (c) fixing a stretched working-capital cycle (receivables ~200+ days, consolidated cash flow at -INR 47 cr).

Inventory & receivable jumps are partly Apiqo/Bizotic opening stock to be liquidated in Q1 FY27. "Other financial assets" jump = advances paid for new capex equipment (6-8 month lead time).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr (clear order book INR 280-300 cr + ~INR 80-90 cr expected); FY28 ~INR 600-700 cr (later said ~INR 700-800 cr run-rate). 3-yr revenue CAGR ~30%.
- **Peak capacity revenue:** existing consol capacity ~INR 450-500 cr at ~80% util; new Rajkot expansion adds standalone peak ~INR 400-450 cr.
- **Margin:** EBITDA 25-30% (PPT/closing guidance); MD oscillated — said 30-35% mid-call, then settled "conservative ~25% consolidated, won't go below." Apiqo ~22-23% (lower, chemicals); Bizotic ~Anlon level.
- **PAT:** FY27 conservative ~INR 45 cr; realistic 50-55 cr (higher depreciation post-acquisition + new capex).
- **Capex:** INR 130 cr greenfield at existing Anlon (Rajkot) premises — construction start ~end-Jun/early-Jul 2026; commissioning ~Q1 FY28; FY28 util ~50-60% (6-month trial/validation ramp). Funding: INR 65-70 cr term loan (~50-60%) + internal accruals; **no equity dilution planned** (rights issue / promoter unsecured loan as fallback).
- **Cash flow:** consolidated positive by end-FY27.
- **Export mix:** targeting ~60% export contribution in FY27.
- **Pipeline:** 7 new API launches in FY27; 3-5 additional DMF filings FY27; 3 CDMO molecules — 1 commercial by Q3 FY27, other 2 validation by Q2 FY27, commercial Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28.
order book & pipeline:
- Clear FY27 order book INR 280-300 cr (consol) + expected ~INR 80-90 cr more → INR 380-400 cr target.
- 21 DMF filings; 5-6 already supplying regulated markets; 5-7 to be commercialized in FY27.
- Pending filings: Dexketoprofen DMF in Europe (EDQM query awaited, ~2-3 months); Ketoprofen US DMF filed via a customer on Anlon's behalf — timeline slipped (Q2 → possibly Q3/Q4 FY27).
- CDMO: 3 molecules for 2 global innovators; one already supplied validation lots (multiples of 100 kg in March).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Core NSAID APIs/intermediates:** among few Indian/global makers of Loxoprofen Sodium, Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen Trometamol. Only ~2-3 Indian players, ~5-6 global (2 China, 1 Korea). Edge = cracked methylation / Friedel-Crafts chemistry at low landed cost; customers include innovators + top-5/10 generics.
- **Apiqo Organics (acquired ~Jan FY26):** intermediate & fine/specialty chemicals; lower EBITDA (~22-23%); near-full utilization on existing business; backward-integration intermediates to start in spare reactors → benefit from Q2 FY27. Specialty-chemical talks with 1-2 customers for dedicated capacity buyout.
- **Bizotic Life Science (FY26):** secures backward-integration supply chain (Anlon was already manufacturing there 3-4 yrs); margins ~Anlon level.
- **Remember Pharma (FY27):** formulation/FDF plant — not in this PPT (acquired in FY27); supports regulated-market FDF + planned peptide manufacturing.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **CDMO:** 3 innovator molecules → first commercial Q3 FY27; scalable custom-manufacturing platform thesis.
- **Industrial & fine / specialty chemicals (via Apiqo):** early traction; possible dedicated-capacity offtake; material contribution expected in 3-6 months.
- **Formulations (FDF) + peptides:** Remember Pharma + planned acquisitions in marketing/distribution of finished dosage for regulated markets.
- **Regulated-market shift:** target ~60% export contribution FY27 (better margins than domestic).
- **Inorganic:** more acquisitions in pipeline (FDF marketing/distribution, peptides); fundable via internal/promoter funds, not immediate.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 margin compression = RM/solvent/catalyst inflation (>100% on many inputs from "war/geopolitical" disruption) vs fixed legacy POs + higher operating cost from two newly-acquired facilities + development expense.
- Repricing underway (treated as force majeure); MD expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA to recover toward prior full-year level. Export/regulated mix carries higher margin than domestic; backward integration (Apiqo intermediates from Q2) to aid profitability.
- Solvent/RM prices now "validity of one day" — high volatility; B2B pass-through lags as it cascades down the chain.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- INR 130 cr greenfield at Rajkot (existing Anlon premises); layout under approval (~mid-month), construction start end-Jun/early-Jul 2026; commissioning Q1 FY28; standalone peak ~INR 400-450 cr.
- New QC + some equipment already installed in existing facility; advances paid (8-month lead times) sitting in "other financial assets" until capitalized.
- Funding: INR 65-70 cr term loan + internal accruals; cash-credit/rights-issue as working-capital fallback.
capital allocation:
- Stock split + bonus done to boost liquidity / shareholder count (~11,000 → ~25,000; target 100k-150k).
- No equity dilution intended for capex; promoter willing to infuse unsecured loans; rights issue preferred over preferential/private placement if needed.
- Acquisition appetite continues (FDF/peptide) but discretionary.
risks & watch-items:
- **Working capital:** receivables ~200+ days (mgmt benchmark ~180 for API; admits ~130-140 average); ~INR 100 cr receivables ≈ 60% of sales; consol operating cash flow -INR 47 cr. New strict 120-day stop-supply policy; positive CF promised by FY27-end — KEY proof point.
- **Legacy bad-ish receivable:** lost a distributor (~INR 20-30 cr stuck flagged Nov-2025); INR 11 cr recovered, ~INR 17 cr outstanding — "not defaulted."
- **Raw-material volatility:** >100% input inflation; ability to fully reprice is the swing factor on margin.
- **Margin guidance wobble:** MD gave 30-35%, then 25-30%, then "~25% conservative" within one call — model on lower end.
- **Acquisition integration:** three acquisitions in ~12 months; consolidation of Apiqo/Bizotic minority (share swap) pending AGM.
- **Credit rating flag:** CARE marked "issuer not cooperating" (historical dispute since 2018-19, MD disputes CARE's conduct); Brickwork withdrew BB-; fresh Brickwork rating expected ~BBB- within 45 days — verify.
- **Execution dependence:** FY28 700-800 cr target needs new facility on time + working-capital funding + DMF commercializations.
management quality / tone: - Single-voice call (MD only); candid and granular on numbers, receivables, the CARE dispute, and Q4 margin causes. Some hesitancy/inconsistency on EBITDA guidance and a deferred tax-rate question (to be answered offline). Confident, slightly promotional on the FY28 doubling and acquisition cadence; anchors guidance to existing customer projections. Audio issues truncated several questions (Remember Pharma answer promised offline).
non-obvious takeaways:
- Real story is a roll-up: NSAID API specialist → backward-integrated (Bizotic/Apiqo intermediates) → forward into FDF/formulations (Remember Pharma) + CDMO + specialty chemicals — building a vertically-integrated platform, not just an API maker.
- Q4 PAT drop is largely transient cost-pass-through lag, not demand — pharma demand "increased vs pre-war"; the durable question is working capital, not the P&L.
- The genuine moat is process chemistry (methylation, Friedel-Crafts) on niche NSAIDs with only 2-3 Indian / 5-6 global players — pricing/cost edge + innovator + top-generic customers + 21 DMFs.
- A listed large pharma customer is reportedly delaying payments despite Anlon's MSME 45-day status; Anlon leverages being on the customer's DMF (hard to switch) to enforce terms — shows niche supplier stickiness.
- Microcap with stretched cash conversion entering a leveraged capex + acquisition phase — execution and WC discipline (not order book) are the binding constraints.

identity.name: ANLON HEALTHCARE LIMITED
identity.industry: Pharma API & Intermediates (NSAID specialist) + emerging Fine/Specialty Chemicals & CDMO

hero.oneLiner: Anlon delivered a strong FY26 (total income +43% to INR 172 cr, EBITDA +48% to INR 47.8 cr, PAT +42% to INR 29.1 cr) and bolted on three acquisitions (Apiqo, Bizotic, and FY27's Remember Pharma) to build a backward-integrated NSAID-API + intermediates + CDMO + formulations platform — but Q4 PAT fell YoY (INR 11.1 cr vs INR 16.7 cr) as a raw-material/solvent cost spike ("war situation", prices >2x) hit B2B contracts already priced at old rates, compressing margins. The story now hinges on (a) repricing customers and restoring the ~25-30% EBITDA band, (b) ramping consolidated capacity (1,400-1,600 MTPA) plus a new INR 130 cr Rajkot greenfield (commissioning ~Q1 FY28) toward a 30% revenue CAGR (FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr, FY28 ~INR 700-800 cr), and (c) fixing a stretched working-capital cycle (receivables ~200+ days, consolidated cash flow at -INR 47 cr).
hero.industry: Pharma API & Intermediates (NSAID specialist) + emerging Fine/Specialty Chemicals & CDMO

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Incorporated in 2013 and based in Rajkot, Gujarat, described as "a research-driven chemical manufacturer" of high-purity advanced pharmaceutical intermediates used as key starting materials for APIs, and of APIs that serve as raw materials for finished dosage formulations.
- Claims to be "Among the few Indian manufacturers of Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate, Ketoprofen & Dexketoprofen Trometamol", key APIs used for pain and inflammation, and "one of the few manufacturers of this APIs in India" for Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate specifically.
- "Strong global presence across 15 countries, serving pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, personal care, and animal health sectors"; 125 customers served till date (directly and indirectly) and 105 employees.
- Regulatory position framed as the moat: 21 DMFs filed with regulators across major international markets, CEP approval from EDQM (Europe) for Ketoprofen, and DMF approvals from ANVISA (Brazil) and NMPA (China) for Loxoprofen Sodium Dihydrate; DMF submissions for Ketoprofen in the USA and Dexketoprofen Trometamol in key European jurisdictions are in progress with approval "expected in a couple of years".
- Competitive edge slide cites "High Entry Barriers and Strong Quality Systems", "High-compliance manufacturing with strong DMF/GMP credentials and 33 approvals, with zero order cancellations", and 4 in-house R&D centres with QA/QC support.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Apiqo Organics Private Limited — subsidiary: 55.06% shareholding; became subsidiary w.e.f. January 09, 2026; related-party sales-of-goods counterparty at arm's length
- Bizotic Lifescience Private Limited — subsidiary: 52.59% shareholding; became subsidiary w.e.f. March 20, 2026; related-party sales-of-goods counterparty at arm's length
- Remember India Health Links Private Limited — subsidiary: 56.83% shareholding; became subsidiary w.e.f. May 08, 2026
- Anlon Medicare Private Limited — subsidiary: 55% shareholding; became subsidiary w.e.f. July 09, 2026
- Anlon Biologics Private Limited — subsidiary: 65% shareholding; became subsidiary w.e.f. July 10, 2026

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Core NSAID APIs/intermediates:** among few Indian/global makers of Loxoprofen Sodium, Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen Trometamol. Only ~2-3 Indian players, ~5-6 global (2 China, 1 Korea). Edge = cracked methylation / Friedel-Crafts chemistry at low landed cost; customers include innovators + top-5/10 generics.
- **Apiqo Organics (acquired ~Jan FY26):** intermediate & fine/specialty chemicals; lower EBITDA (~22-23%); near-full utilization on existing business; backward-integration intermediates to start in spare reactors → benefit from Q2 FY27. Specialty-chemical talks with 1-2 customers for dedicated capacity buyout.
- **Bizotic Life Science (FY26):** secures backward-integration supply chain (Anlon was already manufacturing there 3-4 yrs); margins ~Anlon level.
- **Remember Pharma (FY27):** formulation/FDF plant — not in this PPT (acquired in FY27); supports regulated-market FDF + planned peptide manufacturing.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Clear FY27 order book INR 280-300 cr (consol) + expected ~INR 80-90 cr more → INR 380-400 cr target.
- 21 DMF filings; 5-6 already supplying regulated markets; 5-7 to be commercialized in FY27.
- Pending filings: Dexketoprofen DMF in Europe (EDQM query awaited, ~2-3 months); Ketoprofen US DMF filed via a customer on Anlon's behalf — timeline slipped (Q2 → possibly Q3/Q4 FY27).
- CDMO: 3 molecules for 2 global innovators; one already supplied validation lots (multiples of 100 kg in March).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~INR 380-400 cr (clear order book INR 280-300 cr + ~INR 80-90 cr expected); FY28 ~INR 600-700 cr (later said ~INR 700-800 cr run-rate). 3-yr revenue CAGR ~30%.
- **Peak capacity revenue:** existing consol capacity ~INR 450-500 cr at ~80% util; new Rajkot expansion adds standalone peak ~INR 400-450 cr.
- **Margin:** EBITDA 25-30% (PPT/closing guidance); MD oscillated — said 30-35% mid-call, then settled "conservative ~25% consolidated, won't go below." Apiqo ~22-23% (lower, chemicals); Bizotic ~Anlon level.
- **PAT:** FY27 conservative ~INR 45 cr; realistic 50-55 cr (higher depreciation post-acquisition + new capex).
- **Capex:** INR 130 cr greenfield at existing Anlon (Rajkot) premises — construction start ~end-Jun/early-Jul 2026; commissioning ~Q1 FY28; FY28 util ~50-60% (6-month trial/validation ramp). Funding: INR 65-70 cr term loan (~50-60%) + internal accruals; **no equity dilution planned** (rights issue / promoter unsecured loan as fallback).
- **Cash flow:** consolidated positive by end-FY27.
- **Export mix:** targeting ~60% export contribution in FY27.
- **Pipeline:** 7 new API launches in FY27; 3-5 additional DMF filings FY27; 3 CDMO molecules — 1 commercial by Q3 FY27, other 2 validation by Q2 FY27, commercial Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **CDMO:** 3 innovator molecules → first commercial Q3 FY27; scalable custom-manufacturing platform thesis.
- **Industrial & fine / specialty chemicals (via Apiqo):** early traction; possible dedicated-capacity offtake; material contribution expected in 3-6 months.
- **Formulations (FDF) + peptides:** Remember Pharma + planned acquisitions in marketing/distribution of finished dosage for regulated markets.
- **Regulated-market shift:** target ~60% export contribution FY27 (better margins than domestic).
- **Inorganic:** more acquisitions in pipeline (FDF marketing/distribution, peptides); fundable via internal/promoter funds, not immediate.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Q4 margin compression = RM/solvent/catalyst inflation (>100% on many inputs from "war/geopolitical" disruption) vs fixed legacy POs + higher operating cost from two newly-acquired facilities + development expense.
- Repricing underway (treated as force majeure); MD expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA to recover toward prior full-year level. Export/regulated mix carries higher margin than domestic; backward integration (Apiqo intermediates from Q2) to aid profitability.
- Solvent/RM prices now "validity of one day" — high volatility; B2B pass-through lags as it cascades down the chain.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Stock split + bonus done to boost liquidity / shareholder count (~11,000 → ~25,000; target 100k-150k).
- No equity dilution intended for capex; promoter willing to infuse unsecured loans; rights issue preferred over preferential/private placement if needed.
- Acquisition appetite continues (FDF/peptide) but discretionary.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26 the company expanded inorganically by acquiring 67.48% equity shareholding in Apiqo Organics Private Limited (subsidiary w.e.f. January 09, 2026) and 56.67% equity shareholding in Bizotic Life Science Private Limited (subsidiary w.e.f. March 20, 2026).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Strategic initiatives slide is off-domain and unbound] The "Strategic Initiatives (Key Growth Catalysts in next 24-36 Months)" slide carries text on recycling and refurbishing spent batteries to recover Li, Co, Ni and Mn through black mass production, repairing and restoring outdated electronics for resale, environmentally responsible dismantling of obsolete electronic products, and end-to-end compliance support under E-Waste Management Rules 2022 - sitting alongside four pharma headings (Portfolio Diversification and Expansion; Expand Customer Base and Wallet Share; Improve cost management & operational efficiencies; New Product Development & DMF Filing for Regulatory). The deck does not explain the link and the text-to-heading binding is not recoverable from the extract, so no battery-recycling or e-waste business is asserted here.
- [Business model shift] The Remember India acquisition is framed as a "Transition from an API-focused manufacturer to an integrated pharmaceutical company" with entry into FDFs and "Presence across B2B APIs, domestic retail and hospital markets" - a change in business model, not just capacity.
- [Customer concentration disclosure] Top 5 and Top 10 customer revenue is disclosed only by segment split, not as a share of total revenue: FY26 slices 28.43% / 69.10% / 2.47% (Top 5) and 28.42% / 69.40% / 2.18% (Top 10), and Q1FY27 43.41% / 43.87% / 5.58% (Top 5) and 47.47% / 43.93% / 5.58% (Top 10) against labels APIs / Pharmaceutical Intermediate / Nutraceutical; label-to-value binding is again not recoverable, and the deck never states what proportion of revenue the top customers represent.
- [Stale forward-looking text] The "Future Growth Roadmap for APIs" slide, in a presentation for Q1 FY-27, still says the APIs-intermediates mix "will be driving stronger revenue momentum in FY26" and calls the initiative "a clear near-term growth catalyst for FY26 and beyond" - the horizon appears carried over from an earlier deck.
- [Market data] Stock data as on 04-08-2026 (source BSE): share price INR 14.58, market capitalization INR 774.95 crore, 53,15,15,000 shares outstanding, face value INR 2.00, 52-week high INR 17.20 and low INR 8.70; shareholding 52.68% Promoter and Promoter Group, 47.32% Public.
